We need to fix ambiguous constructor call for TSIG nullAlgKey line. There are two constructors: TSIG(Name, Name, String) and TSIG(Name, String, String). The test intends to pass null algorithm Name, using constructor with Name for name, Name for algorithm, and secret string. But passing null for algorithm ambiguous because both constructors accept (Name, ?, String). To disambiguate, we can cast null to Name, e.g., (Name) null. So change line:

TSIG nullAlgKey = new TSIG(Name.fromString("nullalg.example."), null, "secret");

to:

TSIG nullAlgKey = new TSIG(Name.fromString("nullalg.example."), (Name) null, "secret");

But also need import Name? Already used earlier. Name class is org.xbill.DNS.Name.

Also ensure other ambiguous calls? Search for similar ambiguous uses. In earlier code, they used new TSIG("example.com.", "hmac-md5", "ABCD...") which is String,String,String. That's fine.

In test setTSIG_nullAlgorithm_handling_resultsInFailure, they also use TSIG nullAlgKey = new TSIG(Name.fromString("nullalg.example."), null, "secret"); That's the only ambiguous.

Thus modify that test.

Also ensure compilation passes: need to import Name? Already used earlier but not imported explicitly. The file imports java.util.List etc., but not Name. However Name is referenced in code; maybe there is a static import? No. So need to import org.xbill.DNS.Name. This file currently does not import Name. It uses Name in several methods: tsigName, tsigAlgorithm, etc. So compilation would have failed earlier due to missing import. However maybe there is a wildcard import? Not. So we need to add import org.xbill.DNS.Name; Also DClass, Section, Header, Record, ARecord, NSRecord, TXTRecord, etc. Those also need imports. The code uses them but not imported. So compile errors would be many. But maybe they are in same package org.xbill.DNS, and the test class is also in that package, so they are accessible without import because same package. Indeed the test class is in package org.xbill.DNS; thus classes in same package are accessible without import. So Name is also in same package; fine.

Thus only ambiguous constructor.

Make change.

Also ensure null algorithm case: the test expects setTSIG handles gracefully. The TSIG constructor with null algorithm may still throw IllegalArgumentException; but they wrap in new TSIG(Name.fromString(...), null, "secret") which now compiles but may throw IAE at runtime; test expects setTSIG not to propagate exception and result in failure state. That's fine.

Thus final code with corrected line.
